$comment: Dependency edges that no import scan can find, because the two ends are in different
language ecosystems. affected_set.py derives the reverse-dependency closure from Python
imports and pyproject declarations; an edge expressed as a subprocess contract, a CLI
invocation, or a build-time code generator is invisible to it, so it is declared here.
Each entry is read as a SOURCE edge, the same tier as a Python package's
[project.dependencies]: the consumer's shipped output is derived from the target, not
merely exercised by its suite. Changing the target therefore re-tests the consumer.
This map lives in the monorepo rather than in the consuming package because a consumer
may be independently publishable. datrix-vscode packages itself into a .vsix, and
verify-package-contents.mjs fails that build when any archived file names a framework
package -- so the one place this fact must NOT be written is the consumer's own shipped
manifest. Everything about a package that is safe to ship (which files hold its tests,
which script builds them) stays in its package.json under a `datrix` key.
